messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node(s) NotReady detected in cluster 'us-west-2-prod' affecting inference-pool-3. Error rate spike + increased latency observed. Pager sent to #eng-oncall.

sarah: I’m on the page. seeing 502s for some inference routes. dashboard shows 30% of replicas in inference-pool-3 NotReady.

miguel: logs from one affected pod show repeated kubelet disconnects then container restart. attaching snippet.

kevin: posting kubectl output:```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-pool-3 -o wide
ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute.internal   NotReady  3d   10.0.12.34   us-west-2a
ip-10-0-12-35.us-west-2.compute.internal   Ready     4h   10.0.12.35   us-west-2a
```

miguel: journalctl from node ip-10-0-12-34:```
Mar 15 03:12:01 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=32145 GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 03:12:02 kubelet: E0315 03:12:02 kubelet_node_status.go:70] Node not ready: kubelet not responding
Mar 15 03:12:05 containerd: shim containerd-shim started, exit status non-zero
```

anya: saw OOM and CUDA driver errors in the runtime logs for the serving container before the kubelet disconnect. likely a driver/kernel issue causing GPU detach.

kevin: ops-bot triggered autoscaler policy but scale is limited by reserved capacity. Dedicated customers might be impacted.

sarah: quick mitigation: cordon the NotReady node to avoid scheduling, and scale replica counts for inference-pool-3 from 40->60 (if capacity permits) so traffic moves to healthy nodes. I’ll attempt cordon now.

sarah: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-34.us-west-2.compute.internal` -> node cordoned :white_check_mark:

miguel: draining pods may cause transient errors. Suggest update routing to favor healthy AZs first. I can flip routing weight on the edge layer.

kevin: edge routing change applied: traffic to us-west-2a reduced by 40% for inference routes. monitor for errors. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

incident-bot: Metric update: 5min error rate for /v1/generate decreased from 18% -> 9% after cordon and routing weight change. Latency p95 improved from 420ms -> 280ms.

anya: for the node itself, infra-oncall can you check GPU driver version and recent kernel updates? looks like a kernel-driver mismatch could cause GPU to drop.

infra-oncall: looking. No scheduled kernel updates on that host, but I see a recent NVIDIA driver patch rolled to image build 2026.03.14 used by that node. correlating with time of first failures.

miguel: can someone fetch `nvidia-smi -q` output from the node before it crashed? if GPU went away we might see signs.

infra-oncall: `nvidia-smi` returns host unreachable (node NotReady). I requested cloud provider support to check host-level hardware telemetry.

kevin: meanwhile, rolling restart of remaining inference pods in pool to pick healthy nodes and clear any kernel-driver stale state. scheduling a rolling restart with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-pool-3 -n prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName!=ip-10-0-12-34` to avoid the cordoned node.

sarah: executing restart now. Notifying SRE to monitor throttles.

ops-bot: :information_source: Rolling restart started for deployment/inference-pool-3. Estimated time 4m per AZ.

miguel: I captured one container log before restart showing CUDA error:```
[2026-03-15T03:11:59Z] runtime: cuda driver error: initialization failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
[2026-03-15T03:12:00Z] serving: OOM killing model shard 2, signal SIGKILL
```

anya: that looks like dual issue: driver error then OOM cascade as serving retries/allocs accumulate. We should add transient-fallback to smaller model variant for critical customers.

kevin: Product/Support FYI: customers with dedicated capacity may see degraded performance. No full data loss. Opening a customer-impact ticket for top 3 paying customers to notify them.

sarah: Status update 03:21Z -> Rolling restart done in us-west-2b/2c. Error rate now 4%. One node still NotReady (ip-10-0-12-34).

infra-oncall: Cloud provider found host-level GPU ECC error and auto-evacuated VM. We're provisioning replacement VM in same AZ and will reprovision with driver pinned to stable build 2026.02.28.

miguel: keeping an eye on canaries. If replacement node comes up with newer driver we should pin to older driver or ensure compatibility testing.

anya: Action items logged: 1) Reimage/replace node with pinned driver (infra-oncall). 2) Add transient smaller-model fallback route to critical routes (sarah + product). 3) Add alert to detect GPU Xid 79 earlier (miguel). 4) Postmortem assigned to SRE team.

kevin: I’ll draft customer note and coordinate with support. ETA initial customer communication 30m.

sarah: Handoff: I need to step off; miguel you take primary for mitigation and follow through with infra-oncall? I’m leaving a pinned note in incidents channel. :handshake:

miguel: taking over the incident. I’ll coordinate with infra-oncall on replacement node and confirm driver pin. ping me on DM for anything urgent.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated -> error rates back to baseline (~0.5%) at 03:34Z. Node ip-10-0-12-34 remains NotReady and will be marked for reprovision.

infra-oncall: Replacement VM provisioned and deployed with driver 2026.02.28. New node joined cluster and pods scheduled. Observability shows no new GPU detach faults.

miguel: Confirming traffic fully restored to original weights. Monitoring for 1h.

ops-bot: Post-incident checklist created: link to incident ticket INC-2026-00321. Please add notes.

kevin: Thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: miguel (technical), infra-oncall (infrastructure), sarah (customer comms).

miguel: I'll collect logs, timeline, and send a draft postmortem by EOD.

sarah: closing my pagers, great collaboration. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: This thread will auto-archive after 30 days.
